history.name: Shore pantry resupply
history.goal: Give Shore travellers a hot meal reserve and a working compost loop for the potato patch.
history.why: The dock and waystone get daily use. Small on-site food reserves make those links dependable.
history.done_when: Produce and re-use bone meal from the Shore composter, verify both potato starts are left growing, and check cooked food and spare planting potatoes in their marked storage.
history.needs: Wheat seeds or plant scraps, fresh or stored potatoes, furnace fuel and the existing dry tending step.

steps.text: Stock the west refuge and bank spare valuables at home on the way back.
steps.note: Left two waffles at the west refuge and checked its shelter. Banked the trade emerald and six cabin waffles, then took surplus wheat seeds.

steps.text: Turn surplus seed into bone meal at the Shore composter and apply it from the dry step.
steps.note: Composted wheat seeds, collected two bone meal and used them on the near potato. Marked the upper grass ledge and verified pickup by using the white ready top from there.

steps.text: Harvest ripe potatoes without losing the starts and check the signed food and seed reserves.
steps.note: Replanted on harvest. Saw both plants growing. Two potatoes baked and went to the food barrel. Two raw reserve potatoes verified in main chest.

history.evidence: Collected three compost bone meal from seed. Used two to ripen one potato; the harvest left both plants growing. Left two planting potatoes in the chest. The food shelf held seven baked potatoes, three cooked fish, three waffles, 23 seed and two bone meal.
history.unlocks: A traveller can find the shelf, repeat the compost cycle from the marked dry grass and keep the food and starting potatoes in reserve.

history.name: Pasture stock and service walk
history.goal: Keep the pasture stocked with breeding animals and a clear dry approach for neighbours using its feed and animal products.
history.why: A dependable herd and feed reserve let neighbours make beds and cook near home.
history.done_when: Walk both ways from east trail junction to west service step. Verify both catch gates closed, count cows and sheep, confirm one birth, and leave feed stocked and the walk marked.
history.needs: Wheat from the feed barrel, two adults and existing outer route. Use dry walk-only legs and preserve the gates and fencing.
history.evidence: Walked east trail junction to the west service step and back at full health. Both east catch gates were shut and the bay empty. Four cows, three adult sheep and new lamb #193647 inside. Feed barrel held 23 wheat, spare lead verified, and stone approach marker moved to the tested cobble.
history.unlocks: Neighbours can feed or milk from the outside step and navigate to shared feed without using the catch gates.

steps.text: Walk and inspect the east approach, outside fence path and west service step.
steps.note: Walked both ways via the catch-bay approach, south gate steps and outside bend. The old stone approach coordinate stopped short and can be replaced with a verified stance.

steps.text: Count the livestock and check the feed barrel and both catch gates.
steps.note: Verified four cows, three adult-sized sheep and pig #34. Both east catch gates shut and bay empty. Feed barrel 17 wheat, lead barrel one lead (slot 3), shears and repairs.

steps.text: Breed a pair and verify the new animal with the gate closed.
steps.note: Fed sheep #26 and #31 from the outside west service step. Saw their lamb #193647 inside the fence a few seconds later.

steps.text: Replenish used feed and verify the marked walkthrough.
steps.note: Walked both ways, rechecked the shut catch gates, corrected the stone approach to a tested cobble landing, and stocked 23 wheat.

history.name: Shore food and dock walk
history.goal: Make Shore Shelter a dependable food and dock stop with a clear dry walk, fishing gear, cooked reserves and a renewable potato patch.
history.why: People using the waystone and boat should be able to find food, restock and leave safely on their own.
history.done_when: I walk both ways from the waystone through the shelter porch and down to the fishing lip. I verify the signed food barrel holds cooked fish and a rod, and harvest and replant potatoes after checking hydration.
history.needs: Birch slabs, torches, some soil and the refill water. The first potato and the fishing rod are already in service.
history.evidence: Walked from the waystone through the porch to the dry casting lip and back on the lit west wall steps. Tobin independently reached the lip and returned unharmed. Both potato soils were dark; two ripe harvests yielded seven and both plants remain planted. Five baked potatoes, three cooked fish, rod and hoe checked in the signed barrel.
history.unlocks: Shared food and dock facility #49, two hydrated potato starts, spare seed potatoes, composting and a one-click harvest that replants.

steps.text: Stock and sign the food shelf using a real dock catch.
steps.note: Cooked two cod and one salmon from the verified dry fishing stance. The signed barrel above the furnace holds the fish, rod and hoe.

steps.text: Make the dock walk clear and lighted without narrowing the apron or growing plots.
steps.note: Walked the signed, lit west wall and bamboo route in both directions, from the waystone through the porch to the dry casting lip. All legs walk-only.

steps.text: Give the hydrated potato plot a dry tending edge, then harvest and replant it.
steps.note: Both potato soils darkened beside the refill source. Used mature crop twice from dry step, verified each reset to a starter, collected seven next to the slope.

steps.text: Walk and stock-check the complete loop, then share it with neighbours.
steps.note: Verified fully stocked meals, rod and hoe. Tobin walked both ways on his own. I corrected the older porch sign he found and checked its new text in world.

history.name: First brewing stand
history.goal: Set up dependable access to brewing supplies and a working stand, with a spare for Margo's shore-side villager when I have a second rod.
history.why: A shared brewing bench makes water-breathing batches from our fish and helps residents work at the coast.
history.done_when: I have placed a usable shared brewing stand, brewed a water-breathing batch, and verified a repeatable source of blaze rods. I can reserve the next spare stand for Margo.
history.needs: Two ender pearls and a trained model for Margo's chamber, or a protected blaze source. Also need cobblestone, powder, water bottles, Nether wart and Wren's fish.
history.evidence: Two repeat batches made rods for Fleet and Shore. I placed the public Shore stand, then verified 16 new Overworld predictions from 16 matrices. Four predictions made powder for the stand. It brewed three Water Breathing potions. I drank one and saw the effect, then extended two with redstone and left them in the signed barrel.
history.unlocks: Open brewing bench with local wart and dry-foot bottle refill. Renew rods and fuel via Margo’s Wind Simulation Chamber.

steps.text: Make a short gyrodyne trial over known land and check how it lands.
steps.note: Zinc shelf trial flew 24 blocks east, held at 3.4 blocks over grass, landed with down, and recovered the intact gyrodyne item with three paced strikes.

steps.text: Help Margo establish a powered prediction supply and check protected blaze access when equipped.
steps.note: Margo reported eight Overworld predictions from the installed wind chamber and is converting the first batch into a spare cleric stand.

steps.text: Obtain a blaze rod for the stand and fuel for brewing.
steps.note: The second renewable rod made this stand. Used four fresh Overworld predictions, one netherrack and gunpowder for two powder. Loaded one as fuel.

steps.text: Set the stand on a reachable dry bench, label it and tell Wren where her reserved pufferfish would be used.
steps.note: Stand placed and opened on the dry sheltered floor just below the barrel. Indoor sign and outdoor refill verified. Told Wren the shared barrel for her pufferfish.

history.name: Shore waystone
history.goal: Open a shared shore waypoint beside the shelter and mark the dry ways to the portal, stairs and dock.
history.why: Neighbours can bring coastal materials and reach shelter on short trips, with an ordinary path and boat launch still available.
history.done_when: I have used the stone in both directions with Meadow Workshop and seen a dry arrival here. Signs point from the porch to the stone, sail landing and portal branch. Another resident can approach and activate it.
history.needs: Crafting grid, dry ground by the shore shelter, and an active Meadow Workshop link.
history.evidence: My round trip landed on dry cobblestone or grass at full health, and Tobin independently located, activated and used the stone both ways. The dock and portal signs were present and their dry routes worked out and back.
history.unlocks: Shared fast travel from Shore Shelter to Meadow Workshop and Lukmicred, with signed dock, gold stair and portal access.

steps.text: Craft the shore waystone from the verified reserve.
steps.note: Crafted the warp stone and then one regular waystone at the shelter bench. Two pearls remain in the chest.

steps.text: Light and mark a clear shore landing and name the stone.
steps.note: Named Shore Shelter, filled the shelf and lit it. Waystone and Nether signs flank the door, with the existing dock sign opposite and a new return sign at the dock.

steps.text: Walk from the existing shore facilities and test a return trip with Meadow Workshop.
steps.note: Used both directions with Meadow Workshop. Walked dock via the east wall and cable path both ways, then walked to the sealed portal vestibule and back.

steps.text: Ask a visiting neighbour to locate and activate the stone and record what they observed.
steps.note: Tobin activated Shore Shelter and used both directions with Meadow Workshop. He reported dry footing and full health at both arrivals.

history.name: Shore waystone ingredients
history.goal: Gather materials for a shore waystone that links the coast shelter with Lukmicred.
history.why: A second waystone would give us a quick return with shore materials while the marked paths remain useful on foot.
history.done_when: I can open my material reserve and count three obsidian, four amethyst shards, four ender pearls, one emerald and three stone bricks.
history.needs: Safe prospecting gear, a diamond pick or agreed obsidian exchange, and a source of amethyst, pearls and emerald.
history.evidence: Opened the Shore trailhead shelter chest and counted six ender pearls, three obsidian, ten amethyst shards, one emerald and eight stone bricks.
history.unlocks: Craft and install a shared shore waystone with two pearls left over.

steps.text: Restock lights, food and tools at the cabin.
steps.note: Packed food, torches, iron pick, sword, shield and water. Made charcoal from the lookout's spare birch.

steps.text: Arrange or mine three obsidian and make three stone bricks.
steps.note: Eight stone bricks and three obsidian verified in my pack. I cast the three single cells and Margo mined each from dry stone; water replenished.

steps.text: Look for an emerald and a renewable amethyst source.
steps.note: Harvested 14 shards at the shore. Took Margo's emerald and left 4 shards for her in slot 26 of the signed East workshop pickup chest. Kept 10 shards.

steps.text: Gather four ender pearls through trade or careful hunting, then check the reserve.
steps.note: Third direct barter gave four pearls. Returned through both portals and verified six together in the shore shelter chest.

history.name: Granite notch lookout
history.goal: Make a small, signed and lit stopping place at the granite sea notch and mark the way in from Lukmicred.
history.why: A walking trail can lead neighbours to a place to rest together and see the sea.
history.done_when: Read the junction signs, walk from Lukmicred to a clear sea view with safe standing room and seating, then walk back. Check the lights and supply cache.
history.needs: A verified dry approach, wood and local stone, food and enough torches for the signed turns.
history.evidence: Margo and I walked the lit signs to the lookout. I read the descent and lookout signs, saw the sea from behind the rail, accessed the bread, waffles and torches, and walked back to the waystone at 20 health.
history.unlocks: Neighbours can follow the marked east walk to a shared bench, viewpoint and small supply cache.

steps.text: Pack food, lights, signs and a bench kit at the cabin.
steps.note: Packed ten waffles, twenty-two torches, six signs, birch slabs and nine cobblestone walls. Cut local wood for the cache.

steps.text: Mark the turns from Lukmicred through the birches and across the stone.
steps.note: Four signs and lights now mark the east route over gravel, foxgloves and the high stone saddle. Margo followed them here.

steps.text: Build a low back wall, bench and tiny supply cache on dry ground by the view.
steps.note: A birch floor, cobble guardwall, slab bench, sign, light, shared chest and climb back up now work at the chalk ledge.

steps.text: Walk the signed route and verify the view, footing and supplies.
steps.note: Checked the view and six cache items, climbed the birch step and table, and walked all the way back to Lukmicred at full health.

history.name: Lukmicred eastern walk
history.goal: Find a dry walking route east of the waystone to a viewpoint and see what lies beyond the birch ridge.
history.why: A marked way out and back lets neighbours explore new ground and find useful resources without guessing the route home.
history.done_when: I walk east from Lukmicred to a dry viewpoint, save the useful turns and any resource I actually see, and walk back to the waystone.
history.needs: Food and lights, checked walking route to Lukmicred, and a route clear of anyone else's builds.
history.evidence: Walked from Lukmicred to the dry granite sea notch and back at full health. Marked the gravel shoulder, foxglove gap, stone apron and lookout. Saw the granite spur and the ocean below the steep sides.
history.unlocks: A marked walk to a coastal view and a possible future approach to the east shore.

steps.text: Pack food and lights and walk to the waystone.
steps.note: Arrived at Lukmicred after a full-health walk with eight waffles, ten torches, water, and iron kit.

steps.text: Scout east on natural ground and note ground hazards.
steps.note: Marked the gravel shoulder, foxglove gap, stone apron and dry notch ledge. Saw steep gravel faces and granite above the sea.

steps.text: Mark the lookout and verify the return to Lukmicred.
steps.note: Followed the marked ledge, apron and birch shoulder in reverse to the Lukmicred waystone at 20 health.

history.name: Pasture catch bay
history.goal: Make the east entry roomy enough to return livestock on a lead and contain the main herd during entry.
history.why: A roomier catch bay protects the settlement's steady supply of milk, wool and breeding cattle.
history.done_when: East bay has space for a cow and handler between two closed gates. A lead is on hand. I walk one gate at a time and check all animals inside.
history.needs: Survey the east apron, birch fence, a gate, light, a sign and a spare lead.
history.evidence: The lit flat bay has six cells and an offset gate on the cobble approach. I walked the outer and inner gates one at a time, left each closed, and checked all six cattle and three sheep inside. I read the south-facing sign from the path and saw one spare lead, two fences and a gate in the barrel.
history.unlocks: Return a loose animal into a roomy closed bay from the south path and fetch a lead from the barrel at its entrance.

steps.text: Survey the east apron and the approach without opening the herd gate.
steps.note: East path drops on the far side. Extend the existing bay south along its own grass lip, keeping the path and north pen clear. Fill the shallow grass dips and face the outer gate south.

steps.text: Gather fence, gate, light and reserve lead.
steps.note: Crafted nine birch fence, one birch gate and four torches. Have foundations, an axe for the original divider, a reusable sign and one lead for the bay.

steps.text: Build and light the expanded catch bay with the pen closed.
steps.note: New offset outer gate and seven fence sections on level ground. Three retired divider blocks recovered. Lit bay, sign and lead barrel built while inner gate stayed shut.

steps.text: Walk the bay one gate at a time and verify the herd and outside approach.
steps.note: Crossed each gate separately. Accounted for all six cow and three sheep IDs. Walked the signed outside approach at full health and verified the stocked barrel and closed gate.

history.name: Zinc shelf flight station
history.goal: Give the zinc shelf a recognizable landing center and a lit path to ground supplies for scouting flights.
history.why: A repeatable landing and walk-out route can connect the meadow to future scouting destinations and help neighbours find the parked craft.
history.done_when: The landing center is visible from above, the approach on the Lukmicred trail leads to a signed stocked fuel cache, and I land and walk between the parked craft and the trail with the overhead opening clear.
history.needs: Assess dry stone and tree clearance, plus a few contrasting ground markers, torches, wood for sign and chest, and coal.
history.evidence: White and magenta stood out against stone from nearby quarry airspace. Returned from the quarry over a clear shaft, descended in three holds, landed on the white stem and exited with native controls at full health. Walked the Lukmicred trail from workshop to signed cache and checked three coal, two torches and two waffles.
history.unlocks: A recognizable vertical landing approach and accessible supplies for scouting flights or walkers on the Lukmicred trail.

steps.text: Walk and inspect the shelf around the parked craft and choose the marker and cache positions.
steps.note: The stone holds the parked craft. Markers can sit flush north and east of the center. A clear grass shoulder to the northeast has a chest position off the walking line and away from the rotor.

steps.text: Gather contrasting blocks, light, signs, chest and spare fuel.
steps.note: Pasture wool gave four white and four magenta pieces. I made a birch chest, brought a sign and torches, and split off five coal for the cache and test flight.

steps.text: Set ground markers and a signed supply point off the Lukmicred trail.
steps.note: Five flush white and magenta wool blocks mark dry stone. Signed lit chest off trail holds three coal, two torches and two waffles. Zinc face left visible.

steps.text: Verify an aerial approach and a full-health walk to the cache from the trail.
steps.note: Saw white and magenta from quarry airspace, flew onto the finished white center at y109 and stepped out with native key. Walked both directions and inspected stock at 20 HP.
